Commentary.Commentary: We are back with the final session of the first day to begin! The two Umpires walk out to the middle. Steven Smith and Usman Khawaja are the two openers for Australia. The Kiwi skipper, Tim Southee has the new ball and will begin the proceedings with the ball. Let's play...
...Day 1, Session 3...

After a promising start from the Kiwi openers in the first hour, it all went downhill for them. Tom Latham looked solid for his 38 but after his dismissal, they just couldn't build any significant partnerships and kept losing wickets at regular intervals. Kane Williamson on his 100th Test played a couple of lovely shots but couldn't make much impact in the first innings while Tom Blundell also added some crucial runs. No one from the middle order could do much but skipper Tim Southee who is also playing his 100th Test along with Matt Henry built up a crucial 55-run partnership that has helped the hosts to post this total. However, the bowlers will need something really special to stop the Aussies from taking the lead here. The umpires decided to take Tea and we will see Australia's reply in the last session. Join us at 8.15 am IST (2:45 am GMT) to catch all the exciting action in the last session.

An outstanding bowling effort from Australia! Josh Hazlewood leads with a terrific five-wicket haul. They exploited the conditions excellently here. Even though they had to wait for the first breakthrough, they kept going hard at the batters. Pat Cummins should have had the first but Head spilled one early on. However, it was Mitchell Starc who opened the gates for them. After that, Hazelwood took over and caused all sorts of trouble for the Kiwi middle order picking up four wickets in no time including the big one of Kane Williamson. Starc looked a bit out of rhythm but in his second spell, he piled more misery on the hosts with two wickets in consecutive deliveries. The tail wagged a bit too much for the liking of the visitors but it was the skipper who broke that partnership and Hazlewood wrapped things up by completing his fifer.

OUT! CAUGHT BEHIND! Another beauty! Nips it away after pitching on the back of a length on off, Matt Henry stays glued on his crease with no real footwork and swings at it but misses. Oh, wait, Australia have gone for a review here for caught behind as Cameron Green who is stationed at gully believes he has heard something! UltraEdge comes up and shows there's a clear spike when the ball passes through the bat. The on-field decision is overturned. The faintest of outside edges and Alex Carey takes another regular grab behind the wickets. Josh Hazlewood finishes up with a sensational 5-fer and New Zealand are bundled out on a paltry 162. And again, the woes for New Zealand in batting continue with this dramatic collapse. And that will be an early TEA on Day 1.

Commentary.Commentary: We are back for the post-Lunch session to begin! The two umpires make their way out. Kane Williamson will resume his inning and Daryl Mitchell will share the crease with him after the fall of Rachin Ravindra right before the Lunch break. ...Day 1, Session 2...

Right then, after a dominating session, Australia would be eyeing to pile more pressure on the Kiwis and with Kane Williamson out in the middle, New Zealand would want to make a strong comeback with a resilient partnership and contribution from the middle order. Stay tuned, as an engaging second session of play begins soon at 6:10 AM IST (12:40 AM GMT).

On the bowling front, Mitchell Starc and Josh Hazlewood opened for Australia, setting the tone for the Test and maintaining pressure for the initial half-hour. Despite delivering some excellent balls and a missed catch opportunity, the Australian bowlers couldn't make a breakthrough initially. Mitchell Starc seemed a bit off-rhythm and inconsistent. Australia utilized five bowlers in the first session, with Josh Hazlewood appearing the most settled and in form. Mitchell Starc, in his second spell, eventually provided the breakthrough for Australia by dismissing Young with a sensational catch from Mitch Marsh at third slip. Australia claimed another wicket when Josh Hazlewood removed Latham with a superb delivery, inducing him to poke on the defence. Hazlewood bowled a superb second spell as he asked some tough questions to the batters as the ball bounced, jagged, and carried well to the keeper allowing him to bowl at his strengths and also succeeded in dismissing Rachin Ravindra.

LUNCH, DAY 1 - Session Summary -  71 Runs,  25.2 Overs, 3 Wickets. The first attritional session draws to a close as the players take Lunch on Day 1 and Australia would be surely the happier side as they managed to remove both the settled Kiwi openers. The match started steadily, with Will Young and Tom Latham displaying caution and focus in their batting. Tom Latham seemed composed and confident, hitting several boundaries early on, while Will Young encountered challenging deliveries from the Australian seamers and narrowly survived a dismissal when Travis Head missed a catch at short leg. Both batters managed to survive the first hour or so, but just as their partnership was gaining momentum, Will Young departed after scoring 14 runs, followed by Tom Latham, who made a well-constructed 38. Kane Williamson strode to the middle in his 100th Test match, and as always, he stands unbeaten but Rachin Ravindra got out cheaply playing a rough shot just before the break.

OUT! EDGED AND GONE! A loose shot from Rachin Ravindra and Josh Hazlewood gets his second now. This is pitched up and outside off, shaping away, Rachin Ravindra stays in his crease and goes for the flashing drive without much footwork, only managing to get a thick outside edge towards first slip where Usman Khawaja takes a sharp catch. New Zealand loses their third wicket just before the end of the session and that tilts the momentum towards the Aussies. THAT WILL BE LUNCH ON DAY 1!

Commentary.Commentary: The bell has been rung at the Hagley Oval! The Australian players are giving a guard of honor to umpire Marais Erasmus, standing in his last-ever Test match. Tom Latham and Will Young are the two openers for New Zealand. The conditions are a bit overcast and we can expect some swing as Mitchell Starc has the shiny red cherry in his hand. Let's play...

We are moments away from the start of the match, but before that, the players of both sides stride out and line up for their respective national anthems. It will be Australia's first followed by the national anthem of New Zealand.

Australia (Unchanged Playing XI) - Usman Khawaja, Steven Smith, Marnus Labuschagne, Cameron Green, Travis Head, Mitchell Marsh, Alex Carey (WK), Mitchell Starc, Pat Cummins (C), Nathan Lyon, Josh Hazlewood.

New Zealand (Playing XI) - Tom Latham, Will Young, Kane Williamson, Rachin Ravindra, Daryl Mitchell, Tom Blundell (WK), Glenn Phillips, Scott Kuggeleijn, Matt Henry, Tim Southee (C), Ben Sears (In for William O'Rourke).
TOSS - Australia won the coin-flip and Pat Cummins elected to BOWL first.

As New Zealand seeks to revitalize their batting lineup and uphold their bowling standards, they pin their hopes on key players Tim Southee and Kane Williamson as they approach their 100th Test match milestone. Southee's exceptional bowling prowess and Williamson's batting mastery, coupled with his composure and class, are indispensable for New Zealand's aspirations. The team relies on Southee's knack for early breakthroughs, while Williamson's adept batting technique and on-field presence are pivotal for a competitive showing. The question looms, can New Zealand level the series and stop Straya's juggernaut, or will Australia assert their dominance once more? With the anticipation building, a riveting Test match awaits. Stay tuned as the toss and team sheets will be announced shortly.

On the flip side, Australia continue their dominance in the whites as they lead this series by 1-0 and winning the first Test convincingly. In the first innings, the world witnessed a Cameron Green brilliance with the bat. His remarkable performance with the bat was instrumental in propelling Australia to a formidable total 174, which was clearly the difference between the two sides, and propelled 'Straya' to post 383 with some valuable contributions from the openers Khawaja and Smith, along with Mitchell Marsh's 40 down the order. Leading the bowling attack, Nathan Lyon's magic worked wonders as he dismantled the Kiwi batting order and managed to keep New Zealand below the 200-run mark. In the second innings, Australia aimed to increase the pressure further. While their batsmen struggled to form partnerships, their substantial lead bolstered their position in the match. Setting a challenging total, Nathan Lyon once again showcased his spin skills, claiming an impressive 6-wicket haul to dismantle the opposition batting lineup. Australia relentlessly kept the pressure on the Kiwi batters, consistently taking timely wickets and not allowing them any respite throughout the match.

New Zealand, coming off a dominant Test series against Proteas, suffered a humbling defeat by 172 runs at Basin Reserve against Australia. Truth be told, New Zealand's batting performance has been subpar. Batting second, they struggled early on, with half the side back in the pavilion for less than 50 runs. In both innings, their top order found it difficult to produce partnerships and the batters eventually failed to handle Nathan Lyon's spin. Kane Williamson had a forgettable outing and the veteran will be looking to contribute more with the bat. While the middle order showed brief resistance, they failed to make a significant impact. The Kiwi bowling attack put in a decent effort, with Matt Henry taking three wickets in the first innings and Glenn Phillips claiming a five-wicket haul in the second. Chasing a daunting target of 368, only Rachin Ravindra and Daryl Mitchell managed to form a strong partnership, while the rest of the team struggled and collapsed like a pack of cards. The hosts failed to cross the 200-run mark in both innings, resulting in a resounding defeat.

Welcome to our coverage of Day 1 of the second and final Test match between the neighboring rivals New Zealand and Australia. The Hagley Oval in Christchurch is poised to host this thrilling contest, with Australia aiming for another clean sweep following their 3-0 victory in the T20I series whereas, New Zealand will be aiming to level the series and save from being humbled.
